description: Security fixes skip the Monday schedule but not the 3-day age floor.
`pnpm-workspace.yaml` sets pnpm's `minimumReleaseAge` to 3 days, and
pnpm enforces it both when resolving and at `--frozen-lockfile`
install. A Renovate PR pinning anything younger fails to generate its
lockfile at all, so a shorter age here would open PRs that can never go
green. 3 days makes the two gates agree.
The cost is small in practice: these alerts only fire for direct
dependencies, and every advisory this repo has seen was transitive,
fixed by lockFileMaintenance below. For a fix that truly can't wait,
add the exact `name@version` to `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` in
`pnpm-workspace.yaml`.
Weekly, and exempt from Renovate's own stability gate. The only route
for a transitive advisory is this refresh — `vulnerabilityAlerts` only
covers direct dependencies — so how often it lands sets how long the
nightly `security.yml` gate stays red.
With the global 3-day `minimumReleaseAge` applied here, the
`renovate/stability-days` check never cleared: every rebase re-resolved
~1,200 entries and restarted the clock. #193 (2026-07-30) and #241
(2026-08-31) both sat with every CI check green and the gate pending,
and no lockfile PR ever automerged; each was merged by hand or not at
all. Moving to monthly (August 2026) didn't help, and in September the
prod audit gate failed nightly for a week on an in-range svgo fix.
`0` is safe because the age floor moved to pnpm itself:
`pnpm-workspace.yaml` sets `minimumReleaseAge` to 3 days, so the
resolver never writes a version younger than that, and
`--frozen-lockfile` in CI rejects one if it somehow appears. That covers
every entry, not just the direct dependencies Renovate's check sees.

packageRules.description: Auto-merge safe update types when CI is green.

description: Majors always require human review, and are only created once
ticked on the Dependency Dashboard. They never automerge, so left to
open on schedule they sit indefinitely and fill `prConcurrentLimit`
— eight were queued at once in September 2026, enough to block every
patch and minor behind them.

packageRules.description: Astro integrations (sitemap, rss, etc — versioned independently of core).
typescript-eslint parser + plugin MUST share a version.
ESLint plugins — move together to avoid plugin/eslint-core mismatches.
Type definitions — additive, low-risk; group all update types incl. major.

description: Every non-major devDependency update in one weekly PR. With one PR
per package, `prHourlyLimit: 4` inside a window that fit a single
run meant four PRs a week, and they went to the same fast-releasing
tools (html-validate, eslint, globals, @types) every Monday. Slower
ones starved: wrangler sat on 4.123.0 from mid-August while a sharp
advisory waited on it. Placed after the groups above so
it absorbs them for non-majors — typescript-eslint and the eslint
plugins still move together, just inside this group. `@astrojs/check`
is excluded so it stays in `astro core` alongside `astro`.
The `overrides:` floors in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` ride along too: they
pin dev-tooling transitives, and `yaml` appears both there and as a
devDependency, which otherwise meant two PRs for one package.
Production dependencies stay out on purpose: each keeps its own
`fix(deps)` PR, so the changelog records it and a regression in the
shipped site traces to one package. The cost here is that one bad
dev update holds the group back until it is split off.

packageRules.description: GitHub Actions on their own track (digest pins maintained by best-practices preset).

description: Leave `wranglerVersion: '^4.21'` in ci.yml as a range. The deploy
steps' `cloudflare/wrangler-action` probes `pnpm exec wrangler
--version` and reuses the lockfile's wrangler when it satisfies the
range. Pinning it to an exact version (which the github-actions group
above would do, and automerge) breaks that match the moment the two
drift, and the action then installs its own wrangler — outside the
lockfile and pnpm's 3-day age floor, in the step holding
CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN. wrangler moves via package.json instead.
